To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
testosterone metabolism by rat brain microsome is enhanced by phenytoinduced cytochrome P-450 isoforms.

the hydroxylation activity of testosterone in brain microsomes is strongly induced by phenytoine, resulting in the formation of 16α‐OH‐testosterone, 6βOH‐testosterone and androstenediol, which are the major metabolites.

the anti‐epilptic drug phenytyoin induces the expression of specific cytochromes P450 in rat brain microsomal membranes, resulting in a strong increase of the testosterone metabolism to 6α, 6β, 16α, 16β hydroxylation and to the formation of androstenedione.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of exogenous compounds on the brain metabolism and its consequences for the development of the central nervous system.
the identification and characterisation of the P450 enzymes which are involved in the testosterone metabolism in rat brain and which are induced by phenytoinduced.
the metabolism of gonadotrophic steroids and the influence of xenobiotic inducible P450 isoforms on the regulation of brain functions in early brain development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
phenytoin is able to increase the expression of CYP isoforms which catalyse the hydroxylation and the subsequent metabolism of the gonadal hormone testosterone.
the metabolism of testosterone in rat brain is catalysed by different P450 isoforms, some of which are induced by phenytoinin.

the metabolism of testosterone by brain microsomes of phenytoin induced animals is catalysed by several isoforms of the CYP2 family, whereas the metabolism in control animals is catalysedin part by CYP2B isoforms and in part by the constitutive CYP3A.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that phenytoin induces a specific pattern of cytochrome P-450 isoforms in rat brain microsomal fractions which results in an altered metabolism of testosterone in the brain.
the metabolism of testosterone in rat brain is enhanced by xenobiotics like phenytoin which are able to induce specific cytochrome isoforms.
phenytoin induces a strong increase of the hydroxylation activity of testosterone in rat brain, which may be due to an increased expression of CYP isoforms of the subfamilies Cyp2B, 2C and 3A.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is not a static environment.
the brain is a metabolically active organ that is capable of synthesizing steroids de novo and that these steroids may have important functions in brain physiology.
phenytoin induces cytochrome P-450 enzymes in the brain that can alter the metabolism of testosterone.
